findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "find_people" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Find athletes and instructors by name, belt, nationality, team or verified status. Rows carry belt, nationality, team, a W-L record and medal counts. Names are …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_gym, get_event, get_series, get_person, get_event_results, search, read_page · Private data: find_people, get_person, compare_people · Public sink: find_classes · Destructive: find_gyms, search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_gym, get_event, get_series, get_person, get_event_results, search, read_page · Private data: find_people, get_person, compare_people · Public sink: find_classes · Destructive: find_gyms, search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
